content.field_explanation:
@timestamp, Preferred field for all time-based filters and aggregations. Use this when time is involved. Use HONG KONG time as default.
availabilityName, This is the name of the device. Must use grouping when working with InterfaceTable data, Use cardinality (Unique Count) to count how many unique devices are connecting to xxx (xxx depends on the grouping)
availabilityStatus, Indicate the status of the device ( up=1 , down= 0), Use average to calculate the online rate of a device
devicedesc, Store what device is being used. Must be filtered as devicedesc.keyword: Ã¢â¬ÂFirewallÃ¢â¬Â when working on InterfaceTable. 
site, Store all the name of possible site. 
InterfaceTable.Description, Indicate what the device's port is connecting to. Must be filter as "InterfaceTable.Description.keyword": "Internet" when working on InterfaceTable data.
InterfaceTable.InError
InterfaceTable.InTraffic, Cumulative inbound network traffic or bandwith usage of the network (unit: byte), Multiply the max value in the time interval by 8 to convert bytes to bits, then divide by the time interval(in seconds), then **apply serial_diff** to find the avg network traffic of the period of time 
InterfaceTable.OutError
InterfaceTable.OutTraffic, Cumulative outbound network traffic or bandwith usage of the network (unit: byte), Multiply the max value in the time interval by 8 to convert bytes to bits, then divide by the time interval(in seconds), then **apply serial_diff** to find the avg network traffic of the period of time 
InterfaceTable.Status, Indicate the device's port status is up or down (up=1,down=2), Can be used directly without any calculation
Memory_Utilization, Store the percentage of the memory usage (18.0 means 18%), Use the max value within the time interval to get the memory usage rate of the device
SSIDTable.BSSID, BSSID is the MAC address that uniquely identifies each access point, Use cardinality (Unique Count) to count how many unique devices are connecting to xxx (xxx depends on the grouping)
SSIDTable.ESSID, The name of a Wi-Fi network that users see and select to connect
SSIDTable.RxDataBytes, Cumulative inbound traffic data (bytes) specific to each SSID-AP pair, representing only the traffic received by a given SSID on a particular AP., Multiply the max value in the time interval by 8 to convert bytes to bits, then divide by the time interval(in seconds), then apply serial_diff to find the bits per second.
SSIDTable.TxDataBytes, Cumulative outbound traffic data (bytes) specific to each SSID-AP pair, representing only the traffic received by a given SSID on a particular AP., Multiply the max value in the time interval by 8 to convert bytes to bits, then divide by the time interval(in seconds), then apply serial_diff to find the bits per second.
WirelessTable.AP_CPUUsage, Store the percentage of the CPU usage (7.0 means 7%), Use the max value within the time interval to get the CPU usage rate of the access point
WirelessTable.AP_Name, The Access Point name
WirelessTable.Memory_Utilization, Store the percentage of the memory usage that instant (44.0 means 44%), Use the max value within the time interval to get the memory usage rate of the access point
WirelessTable.AP_Status, Indicate the status of the Access Point (1=Up, 2=Down, 7=Lower Layer Down), Can be used directly without any calculation
WirelessTable.AP_MACAddress, MAC address of the access point
ClientTable.MACAddress, Store each [client deviceâs] unique MAC (Media Access Control) address, Use cardinality (Unique Count) to count how many clients are connecting to an access point
ClientTable.ReceivedByte, Culmulative inbound network traffic to a client's device (unit: byte), Multiply the max value in the time interval by 8 to convert bytes to bits, then divide by the time interval(in seconds), then apply serial_diff to find the bits per second.
ClientTable.TransmitByte, Culmulative outbound network traffic to a client's device (unit: byte), Multiply the max value in the time interval by 8 to convert bytes to bits, then divide by the time interval(in seconds), then apply serial_diff to find the bits per second.
ClientTable.SignalToNoiseRatio, ratio of the signal power to the noise power(Higher values mean a cleaner, higher-quality signal), Use the max value within the time interval to get the signal noise ratio
